title: Calciphylaxis
diseaseDescription: Calciphylaxis (calcific uraemic arteriolopathy): ischaemic skin necrosis from calcification, intimal thickening and thrombosis of small cutaneous arterioles, mainly in people on dialysis. This bounded map covers dialysis and clinical risk factors (phosphate, calcium load, PTH, obesity, diabetes, corticosteroids, hypoalbuminaemia, female sex), calcification-inhibitor deficiency (vitamin K status, warfarin, matrix Gla protein, fetuin-A), vascular smooth-muscle osteogenic change, arteriolar calcification, thrombophilia and microthrombosis, skin necrosis, sepsis and mortality. Most human links are associations from case-control studies and biopsy series; causal links rest on rodent knockout/warfarin models and in vitro work. Contradicting and qualifying results are retained.
releaseNote: Candidate reconciled against calciphylaxis-summary-candidate-9b1e60179c27 (328e540a3c2ba5ec8e4b3ada6c2283f703aa6c6c56a0910bea3f1a7a7ed0090c). 2 extracted findings; independent domain review is pending.

entities.label: Calciphylaxis (clinical syndrome)
entities.description: Calcific uraemic arteriolopathy: painful cutaneous ischaemia and necrosis with medial calcification of cutaneous arterioles.

entities.label: Vitamin K status
entities.description: Vitamin K status; deficiency denotes low status, limiting gamma-carboxylation of Gla proteins.

entities.label: Vitamin K antagonist (warfarin) exposure
entities.description: Exposure to vitamin K antagonists (warfarin, phenprocoumon, acenocoumarol).

entities.label: Matrix Gla protein (carboxylated, active)
entities.description: Vitamin K-dependent extracellular calcification inhibitor; uncarboxylated/dp-ucMGP is the inactive form (low active MGP).

entities.label: Fetuin-A
entities.description: Circulating systemic calcification inhibitor (alpha2-Heremans-Schmid glycoprotein, AHSG).

entities.label: Serum phosphate / hyperphosphataemia
entities.description: Serum or extracellular inorganic phosphate concentration.

entities.label: Vascular smooth muscle cell osteochondrogenic transdifferentiation
entities.description: Osteo/chondrogenic phenotype switch of vascular smooth muscle cells, marked by BMP-2 signalling, Runx2/Cbfa-1, osteocalcin and osteopontin expression.

entities.label: Medial calcification of cutaneous arterioles
entities.description: Medial (mural) calcification of small cutaneous and subcutaneous arterioles, the defining vascular lesion of calciphylaxis.

entities.label: Kidney failure on dialysis (CKD stage 5D)
entities.description: Kidney failure treated with haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis.

entities.label: Calcium load (serum calcium, calcium-based binders)
entities.description: Calcium exposure from serum calcium elevation and calcium-containing phosphate binders.

entities.label: Parathyroid hormone / hyperparathyroidism
entities.description: Parathyroid hormone levels and secondary hyperparathyroidism.

entities.label: Obesity
entities.description: Obesity / higher body mass index.

entities.label: Diabetes mellitus
entities.description: Diabetes mellitus, including insulin-treated diabetes.

entities.label: Systemic corticosteroid exposure
entities.description: Use of systemic glucocorticoids.

entities.label: Hypoalbuminaemia
entities.description: Low serum albumin, a marker of malnutrition/inflammation.

entities.label: Female sex
entities.description: Female sex as a demographic risk marker (no ontology class fits; modelled as clinical attribute).

entities.label: Arteriolar intimal hyperplasia / fibrosis
entities.description: Intimal proliferation/fibrosis narrowing small cutaneous arteries and arterioles.

entities.label: Cutaneous microvascular thrombosis
entities.description: Fibrin/platelet thrombi in dermal and subcutaneous small vessels.

entities.label: Thrombophilia (protein C/S deficiency, antiphospholipid antibodies)
entities.description: Inherited or acquired hypercoagulable states, including lupus anticoagulant, protein C/S and antithrombin deficiency.

entities.label: Systemic inflammation
entities.description: Inflammatory signalling (e.g. IL-6) acting on vascular endothelium.

entities.label: Skin ischaemia, necrosis and ulceration
entities.description: Ischaemic cutaneous lesions of calciphylaxis: plaques, retiform purpura, necrosis and ulceration.

entities.label: Wound infection / sepsis
entities.description: Infection of necrotic wounds and resulting bacteraemia/septicaemia.

entities.label: Mortality
entities.description: Death (all-cause or calciphylaxis-related).

entities.label: Calcium-sensing receptor (parathyroid)
entities.description: G-protein-coupled receptor on parathyroid chief cells that senses extracellular calcium and suppresses PTH secretion; the target of calcimimetics.

entities.label: Circulating pyrophosphate
entities.description: Circulating calcification inhibitor measured in a human calciphylaxis registry; lower levels were associated with case status and outcomes, without establishing causal deficiency.

claims.text: In haemodialysis patients, a lower carboxylated fraction of circulating matrix Gla protein was associated with higher odds of calciphylaxis, each 0.1-unit fall in relative cMGP corresponding to more than a two-fold higher risk; the association persisted in patients not taking warfarin.
limitations: Very small case-control (n=40) from a single programme; wide uncertainty around the risk estimate
MGP measured at or after diagnosis, so reverse causation and illness effects cannot be excluded
Brief report; abstract does not report the full multivariable adjustment set

claims.text: Among the same dialysis patients, vitamin K deficiency was associated with a lower carboxylated fraction of matrix Gla protein in multivariable adjusted analyses, linking vitamin K status to MGP activation rather than to total MGP mass.
limitations: Cross-sectional biomarker association within a 40-patient case-control study; not an intervention
Vitamin K assay and deficiency threshold not described in the abstract
Observational: unmeasured nutritional and inflammatory confounding plausible in dialysis patients

claims.text: In a Japanese nationwide case-control study of biopsy- and clinically-confirmed calciphylaxis in haemodialysis patients, warfarin therapy was strongly associated with calciphylaxis and remained significant after multivariable adjustment (univariate OR 11.4, 95% CI 2.7-48.1).
limitations: Retrospective case-control with 48% centre response rate; selection and recall bias likely
Exposures recorded at the time of diagnosis, so indication bias (atrial fibrillation, vascular disease) cannot be excluded
Wide confidence interval around the warfarin odds ratio; modest sample size

claims.text: Dialysis patients with calciphylaxis in the German registry had median serum fetuin-A well below the assay reference range, indicating depletion of this systemic calcification inhibitor in established calciphylaxis.
limitations: Comparison is against an assay reference range, not against matched dialysis controls (fetuin-A is also low in CKD generally)
Fetuin-A is a negative acute-phase reactant, so low levels may reflect the inflammation and wound burden of established disease
Cross-sectional measurement after diagnosis; no temporal or causal inference possible

claims.text: Skin specimens from calciphylaxis patients showed increased expression of inactive uncarboxylated matrix Gla protein alongside upregulation of BMP-2, Runx2 and sclerostin, compared with dialysis and non-CKD skin controls.
limitations: Very small tissue series (7 cases); semi-quantitative immunohistochemistry
Cross-sectional biopsy of established lesions: cannot separate cause from consequence of calcification
Local Glu-MGP staining may reflect lesional vitamin K consumption rather than systemic vitamin K status

claims.text: The authors interpret calciphylaxis as an active osteogenic process in which upregulated BMP-2/Runx2 signalling in the cutaneous vessel wall accompanies hydroxyapatite deposition and widespread media calcification of cutaneous arterioles.
limitations: Observational human histology: directionality between the osteogenic programme and mineral deposition is inferred, not demonstrated
Only 7 cases; marker expression scored on lesional tissue where calcification is already present
No functional or interventional component

claims.text: In 25 calciphylaxis skin biopsies, osteopontin expression was confined to the subcutis and was most striking in calcified vessels, though it was also present in non-calcified and mineral-poor vessels, suggesting the osteogenic marker is not simply a consequence of mineral deposition.
limitations: Case series without a matched control group of dialysis skin biopsies
Immunohistochemistry scored descriptively, not quantified
Mixed uraemic and non-uraemic cases (renal failure in 21 of 25); cross-sectional

claims.text: In rats, high-dose warfarin produced focal medial calcification of arteries and heart valves resembling the matrix Gla protein-deficient mouse, which the authors attribute to warfarin inhibiting gamma-carboxylation and thus inactivating MGP; serum MGP fell while calcium and phosphorus were unchanged.
limitations: Rat model of warfarin-induced arterial calcification; not human calciphylaxis and no skin or cutaneous arteriolar lesions assessed
Pharmacological warfarin doses far above clinical anticoagulant exposure
The MGP mechanism is inferred from phenotypic similarity to the MGP-deficient mouse rather than tested directly

claims.text: Warfarin administration caused medial calcification of the elastic lamellae of rat arteries within two weeks that progressively increased over five weeks, showing that vitamin K antagonism alone is sufficient to initiate medial arterial calcification.
limitations: Rat large arteries and heart valves, not cutaneous arterioles, and not a calciphylaxis model (no skin necrosis reported)
Supraphysiological warfarin dosing with vitamin K co-administration
Species differences in MGP handling and mineral metabolism limit transfer to human dialysis patients

claims.text: Mice lacking matrix Gla protein develop spontaneous arterial and cartilage calcification and die of blood-vessel rupture within two months, establishing MGP as an active inhibitor of soft-tissue and arterial calcification produced by vascular smooth muscle cells.
limitations: Mouse germline knockout of total MGP; not human calciphylaxis and not a model of cutaneous arteriolar disease
Phenotype involves large elastic arteries and cartilage rather than cutaneous arterioles
Complete lifelong MGP absence is a more extreme perturbation than the partial undercarboxylation seen in dialysis patients

claims.text: Fetuin-A (Ahsg)-deficient mice develop severe ectopic calcification of multiple organs on a mineral- and vitamin D-rich diet without changes in calcium or phosphate homeostasis, identifying fetuin-A as a systemically acting inhibitor of ectopic calcification.
limitations: Mouse knockout with dietary mineral challenge; not human calciphylaxis and cutaneous arteriolar calcification was not the reported phenotype
Organ-level ectopic calcification described generically rather than specifically in skin arterioles
The link to calciphylaxis is the authors inference, not a tested outcome

claims.text: Elevated extracellular phosphate dose-dependently induced mineralisation of cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells and enhanced expression of the osteoblastic differentiation markers osteocalcin and Cbfa-1 (Runx2), through the sodium-dependent phosphate cotransporter Pit-1.
limitations: In vitro study of CKD-type vascular calcification in human aortic smooth muscle cells; not calciphylaxis and not cutaneous arteriolar cells
Cultured cells in high-phosphate media do not reproduce the inhibitor-replete, flowing in vivo environment
No clinical or histological calciphylaxis outcome measured

claims.text: In the ANZDATA registry (2019-2022), calciphylaxis occurred in patients on kidney replacement therapy at an incidence of about 4.5 episodes per 1000 patient-years on dialysis.
limitations: Registry-reported cases; diagnosis not centrally adjudicated and likely under-reported
Describes incidence within dialysis; no non-dialysis comparator incidence, so dialysis is a setting rather than a quantified relative risk

claims.text: In a single-centre Chinese matched case-control study of haemodialysis patients, higher serum phosphate was an independent risk factor for calciphylaxis after multivariable analysis.
limitations: Very small sample; wide confidence intervals
Retrospective; laboratory timing relative to onset not standardised in abstract
Association only

claims.text: In the Japanese nationwide case-control study, serum phosphate and calcium-phosphate product were not significantly associated with biopsy-confirmed calciphylaxis in haemodialysis patients.
limitations: Small number of definite cases limits power to detect associations
Null finding may reflect Japanese practice patterns (tight phosphate control)

claims.text: In a small peritoneal dialysis case-control study, cumulative calcium carbonate (calcium salt) ingestion showed a trend toward increased calciphylaxis risk, which the authors interpreted as calcium ingestion being a risk factor.
limitations: Only 8 cases; the calcium carbonate association was a non-significant trend (p about 0.056)
Peritoneal dialysis population only
Result details partly lost to pipeline normaliser after a literal '<' in the abstract; quote taken from conclusion

claims.text: In a large-dialysis-organisation matched case-control study (1030 incident CUA cases), higher serum calcium, phosphorus and parathyroid hormone at haemodialysis initiation were associated with later calciphylaxis.
limitations: Case ascertainment from clinical records (not uniformly biopsy-proven)
Baseline values measured a median of ~2.5 years before CUA; residual confounding possible
Association only

claims.text: In the German calciphylaxis registry, median intact PTH in dialysis CUA patients was only moderately raised (147 pg/mL) and the authors concluded uncontrolled hyperparathyroidism is not the key determinant of calciphylaxis.
limitations: Descriptive registry without a control group; no formal risk estimate for PTH
Voluntary notification; selection bias possible

claims.text: In the Japanese nationwide case-control study, higher adjusted serum calcium at diagnosis was associated with calciphylaxis in univariate analysis (warfarin and low albumin were the multivariable risk factors).
limitations: Univariate association; serum calcium not reported as an independent risk factor after multivariable adjustment
Calcium measured at diagnosis; reflects serum calcium rather than binder exposure

claims.text: In the Mayo Clinic series, obesity was identified as a risk factor for calciphylaxis in dialysis patients compared with age- and sex-matched dialysis controls.
limitations: Retrospective single centre
Risk factor analysis restricted to dialysis subset; no controls for 15 non-dialysis cases

claims.text: In the same Mayo Clinic matched dialysis analysis, systemic corticosteroid use was associated with calciphylaxis.
limitations: Retrospective single centre; dose and timing of corticosteroid exposure not given in abstract
Confounding by underlying inflammatory disease possible

claims.text: Diabetes was associated with later calciphylaxis in the large US dialysis case-control study, and insulin-treated patients showed a dose-response increase in odds of CUA at typical injection sites (abdomen/thigh).
limitations: Observational; injection-site trauma interpretation is the authors' hypothesis
Insulin use is also a marker of diabetes severity and obesity

claims.text: In the Japanese nationwide case-control study, lower serum albumin remained a significant risk factor for calciphylaxis after multivariable adjustment.
limitations: Albumin measured at diagnosis, so may reflect illness/inflammation (reverse causation)
Small number of cases

claims.text: In a US case-control study of end-stage kidney disease patients, women had about sixfold higher odds of calciphylaxis; low albumin and higher phosphate were also associated.
limitations: Small sample; wide confidence interval
Not replicated in all populations (Chinese and Japanese case-control studies found no female excess)

claims.text: In paired biopsies of lesional and clinically normal skin from 18 patients with suspected calciphylaxis (mostly dialysis), microvascular thrombosis was found only in lesional tissue.
limitations: Small study (n=18) acknowledged by authors
Suspected rather than uniformly confirmed calciphylaxis
Cross-sectional histology cannot establish temporal order of thrombosis and necrosis

claims.text: Intimal hyperplasia of small arteries/arterioles was confined to lesional skin and, together with thrombosis and coarse vascular calcification, was judged a specific finding in suspected calciphylaxis.
limitations: Small study (n=18)
Authors' 'pathogenic role' is an inference from co-occurrence, not tested
Intimal hyperplasia co-occurred with calcification and thrombosis in most samples, so independent contribution unclear

claims.text: Small-artery/arteriolar calcification was nearly as common in clinically normal skin as in lesional skin of the same patients; only coarse calcification was lesion-specific, so vascular calcification alone lacked specificity for necrotic lesions.
limitations: Small study (n=18)
Control tissue from the same high-risk patients, not healthy controls

claims.text: Skin biopsies from patients with calciphylaxis (n=57) were significantly more likely than biopsies from ESRD patients without calciphylaxis (n=26) to show dermal vessel calcification and diffuse dermal thrombi; histology was indistinguishable between patients with and without CKD, suggesting a common pathway in uraemic and non-uraemic calciphylaxis.
limitations: Retrospective, single cohort
Control biopsies taken for other indications (not matched sites)
Effect sizes not given in abstract

claims.text: Compared with viable skin from amputation margins of ESRD patients without calciphylaxis, skin biopsies taken for suspected calciphylaxis showed significantly more small-vessel thrombosis, whereas calcification prevalence did not differ overall.
limitations: Biopsies were for suspicion of calciphylaxis, not all confirmed
Amputation sites differ anatomically from typical biopsy sites
Small sample

claims.text: Medial calcification and other historically 'characteristic' findings also occurred in viable skin of ESRD patients without calciphylaxis; only the combination of medial calcification with thrombosis was rare in unaffected patients (six-fold more prevalent in high-suspicion biopsies).
limitations: Calcification was more common in the high-clinical-suspicion subgroup, so the null overall comparison partly reflects diagnostic uncertainty
Small sample

claims.text: In a two-centre case-control study of patients with renal disease (38 calciphylaxis cases, 114 matched CKD controls), lupus anticoagulant, protein C deficiency and combined thrombophilias were more frequent in calciphylaxis cases.
limitations: Thrombophilia testing done clinically, not systematically; denominators small and variable
Acquired protein C deficiency may reflect warfarin, liver disease or the illness itself
Temporal relationship to calciphylaxis onset unclear

claims.text: Restricting to stage 5 CKD, only lupus anticoagulant and combined thrombophilia remained associated with calciphylaxis (protein C deficiency did not), and in warfarin-unexposed patients only lupus anticoagulant and protein C deficiency remained; the associated thrombophilia component varies by subgroup.
limitations: Very small subgroups; multiple comparisons
Subgroup counts as printed in the abstract are internally inconsistent

claims.text: In a single-centre prospective series of 36 calciphylaxis cases, six-month mortality was 33% in patients presenting with non-ulcerating plaques and rose to above 80% once ulceration developed.
limitations: Small series; unadjusted descriptive comparison
Clinical (largely non-biopsy) diagnosis
Ulceration may mark more advanced or severe disease rather than independently cause death

claims.text: In the UK Calciphylaxis Study, haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis had substantially higher all-cause mortality than propensity-matched haemodialysis patients without calciphylaxis (annual mortality 67% vs 10.2%).
limitations: Registry with voluntary enrolment
Residual confounding possible despite propensity matching
Causes of death not detailed in abstract

claims.text: In a 13-centre Malaysian dialysis cohort of 33 confirmed calciphylaxis cases, about half died within three months of diagnosis and septicaemia from infection was the most frequent cause of death.
limitations: Small descriptive cohort without comparison group
Source of sepsis (wound vs other) not specified in abstract
Cause-of-death attribution from medical records

claims.text: Sera from patients with uraemic calciphylaxis induced IL-6 and IL-6R synthesis in primary human dermal microvascular endothelial cells; TYMP-driven IL-6 activated tissue factor, a trigger of the extrinsic coagulation pathway, which anti-IL-6 treatment inhibited, and calciphylaxis skin showed increased IL-6 signalling.
limitations: Endpoint is endothelial tissue-factor induction in vitro, not observed thrombosis
IL-6 signalling is largely local (lesional microenvironment) rather than demonstrated systemic inflammation
Serum effect may reflect uraemia generally; comparison groups not detailed in abstract

claims.text: In vitro, SNF472 bound hydroxyapatite with micromolar affinity, inhibited HAP crystal formation and inhibited calcification of rat vascular smooth muscle cells, with free-calcium chelation only at ~50-fold higher concentrations.
limitations: Not human calciphylaxis tissue; rat VSMCs and cell-free assays (evidenceType human_in_vitro used as the closest allowed in-vitro category).
Sponsor-authored pharmacology study.
An erratum (PMID 37161658) is linked to this paper; content of the erratum not inspected.

claims.text: In a single-arm open-label phase 2 study of 14 haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis, improvements from baseline in wound score (BWAT), pain and wound-related quality of life were observed after 12 weeks of SNF472.
limitations: No control group; change from baseline on background care cannot be attributed to the drug.
Small sample (n=14); subsequent placebo-controlled phase 3 (CALCIPHYX) did not confirm superiority.
Results section numerics lost to the pipeline "<" normaliser defect; quote taken from Conclusions.
Sponsor-funded.

claims.text: In the phase 3 CALCIPHYX RCT (n=71), wound score (BWAT-CUA) and pain VAS improved similarly with hexasodium fytate and placebo at week 12 (BWAT-CUA LS mean difference 0.3, p=0.88; pain VAS difference 11.5, p=0.15); neither primary endpoint was met.
limitations: Small trial (37 vs 34 randomised); limited power.
Background care (which could include sodium thiosulfate) was permitted, possibly diluting the effect.
Sponsor-funded.

claims.text: In CALCIPHYX, deaths (1/38 vs 5/33 to week 12; 2/38 vs 7/33 over the whole trial) and calciphylaxis-related hospitalisations (2/38 vs 11/33) were fewer with hexasodium fytate than placebo, reported as serious adverse events rather than prespecified efficacy endpoints.
limitations: Safety/serious-adverse-event counts, not a prespecified efficacy endpoint; no formal hypothesis test reported in the abstract.
Very few events; whole-trial counts include an open-label period in which all received drug.
Hypothesis-generating only.

claims.text: CALCIPHYX (NCT04195906) is registered as a completed phase 3 trial (71 enrolled, completed 2022-10-24) assessing SNF472 added to background care for calciphylaxis; supports investigational (experimental) status, not approval.
limitations: Registry status only; does not establish efficacy.
No later calciphylaxis registration for SNF472/CSL525 found; sponsor development decision not verified.

claims.text: In uraemic rats, sodium thiosulfate prevented histological aortic calcification and reduced aortic, cardiac and renal calcium content, likely via acid- and/or chelation-induced urinary calcium loss; it also lowered bone strength.
limitations: Animal model of CKD vascular (aortic) calcification, not human calciphylaxis or cutaneous arterioles.
Prevention design (treatment started before calcification), not treatment of established lesions.
Adverse bone effects and metabolic acidosis observed.

claims.text: Sodium thiosulfate, acting as a hydrogen sulfide donor, inhibited intimal hyperplasia in mouse focal carotid stenosis models and in cultured human vein segments, limiting VSMC proliferation and migration via microtubule depolymerisation.
limitations: Restenosis/revascularisation model, not calciphylaxis; relevance to calciphylaxis arteriolar intimal hyperplasia is inferred.
Oral STS in drinking water in mice, not the intravenous regimen used in calciphylaxis.

claims.text: In 172 haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis treated with IV sodium thiosulfate (Fresenius Medical Care North America, 2006-2009), physician survey (n=53) reported complete resolution in 26.4% and improvement in a further 47.2%; one-year mortality was 35%. The authors state conclusive efficacy evidence is lacking.
limitations: No untreated comparator; uncontrolled response rates cannot be attributed to STS.
Lesion outcomes available only for 53/172 via physician survey; 20.8% of those unknown.
Concomitant therapies not controlled.

claims.text: A phase 3 placebo-controlled RCT of IV sodium thiosulfate for calciphylaxis pain (NCT03150420, Hope Pharmaceuticals) was terminated after enrolling 29, because patients could not be accrued without recent STS exposure; no results posted.
limitations: Registry status only; no efficacy data.
Termination reflects entrenched off-label use, not a safety or efficacy finding.

claims.text: Intravenous sodium thiosulfate 25 g thrice weekly is a placebo-controlled arm of the recruiting phase 3 BEAT-Calci platform trial (NCT05018221) in kidney failure with newly diagnosed calciphylaxis; supports experimental status.
limitations: Ongoing; no results (estimated completion 2029-12).

claims.text: In the iPACK-HD pilot RCT (n=86 haemodialysis patients with coronary calcification), phylloquinone 10 mg thrice weekly for 12 months increased plasma phylloquinone and the Gla/Glu-osteocalcin ratio versus placebo, i.e. improved vitamin K status.
limitations: Not a calciphylaxis population.
Pilot feasibility trial; biomarker outcomes secondary.

claims.text: Phylloquinone supplementation in haemodialysis patients reduced inactive dephospho-uncarboxylated MGP by 86% versus placebo at 12 months, consistent with increased MGP carboxylation (activation); coronary calcification progression did not differ.
limitations: Not a calciphylaxis population; dp-ucMGP is a circulating biomarker, tissue MGP carboxylation not measured.
No effect on coronary calcification progression (clinical calcification outcome null).

claims.text: A pilot RCT of oral vitamin K in calciphylaxis (NCT02278692, MGH) is registered as completed (26 enrolled, 2019-08) with primary outcome change in circulating MGP, but has no posted results and no linked results publication was found.
limitations: No outcome data available; absence of results publication is itself a gap (possible non-publication).

claims.text: Oral vitamin K1 10 mg thrice weekly is a placebo-controlled arm of the recruiting phase 3 BEAT-Calci platform trial (NCT05018221); supports experimental status.
limitations: Ongoing; no results (estimated completion 2029-12).

claims.text: Calcimimetics such as cinacalcet act on the calcium-sensing receptor to lower parathyroid hormone without raising calcium and phosphorus (stated rationale of the phase 3 RCTs in haemodialysis patients).
limitations: Quote is the background statement of mechanism, not a receptor-level experiment in this paper.
Not a calciphylaxis population.

claims.text: In placebo-controlled phase 3 RCTs in haemodialysis patients with uncontrolled secondary hyperparathyroidism, cinacalcet lowered PTH and improved calcium-phosphorus homeostasis over 26 weeks.
limitations: Not a calciphylaxis population; Results numerics lost to the "<" normaliser defect, quote taken from Conclusions.
Industry-funded.

claims.text: In a secondary analysis of adverse-event reports from the EVOLVE RCT (3861 haemodialysis patients with moderate-severe secondary hyperparathyroidism who received study drug), calciphylaxis occurred in 6 cinacalcet vs 18 placebo patients (unadjusted relative hazard 0.31, 95% CI 0.13-0.79).
limitations: Calciphylaxis not a prespecified endpoint; ascertained from investigator adverse-event reports without adjudication described in the abstract.
Events counted only while on study drug (on-treatment), not ITT; unadjusted estimate; 24 events in total.
Prevention of incident calciphylaxis, not treatment of established disease.
Industry-funded (Amgen) parent trial.

claims.text: Within the EVOLVE calciphylaxis cases, active vitamin K antagonist use was common (11 of 24 cases; 9 placebo, 2 cinacalcet) versus 5-7% of patients without calciphylaxis, so imbalance in VKA exposure between arms may confound the apparent cinacalcet effect.
limitations: Descriptive counts among 24 cases; no adjusted analysis for VKA use reported in the abstract.

claims.text: Circulating pyrophosphate was lower in 30 patients with calciphylaxis than in 30 matched controls; lower PPi was associated with higher odds of calciphylaxis after adjustment for ALP, phosphate and BMI.
limitations: Small observational matched case-control study; measurement after diagnosis cannot establish temporal direction or causation.
Only 67% had ESKD; findings must not be treated as a dialysis-only population.
Industry funded, with several authors employed by the sponsor. No PPi-raising intervention was tested.

claims.text: In the calciphylaxis cohort, lower enrollment PPi was associated with higher short-term mortality; PPi also correlated with lesion count but not pain intensity. These observations do not establish that raising PPi improves outcomes.
limitations: Seventy-patient cohort, short follow-up, substantial within-person PPi variability and possible residual confounding.
The adjusted mortality association was reported in the ESKD subgroup; no universal mortality effect is asserted.
No significant association with pain intensity; biomarker association does not demonstrate treatment benefit.

evidenceItems.studySystem: Animal experiment: Ahsg (fetuin-A)-deficient mice on mineral/vitamin D-rich diet and on DBA/2 background, with ex vivo serum mineral-formation inhibition assays

evidenceItems.summary: Elevated extracellular phosphate dose-dependently induced mineralisation of cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells and enhanced expression of the osteoblastic differentiation markers osteocalcin and Cbfa-1 (Runx2), through the sodium-dependent phosphate cotransporter Pit-1.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human in vitro: cultured human aortic smooth muscle cells (HSMCs) exposed to physiological vs hyperphosphataemic phosphate concentrations, with phosphonoformic acid inhibition of the Pit-1 cotransporter

evidenceItems.summary: In the ANZDATA registry (2019-2022), calciphylaxis occurred in patients on kidney replacement therapy at an incidence of about 4.5 episodes per 1000 patient-years on dialysis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Australia/New Zealand binational dialysis and transplant registry; 333 calciphylaxis episodes vs 46,526 KRT patients without calciphylaxis

evidenceItems.summary: In a single-centre Chinese matched case-control study of haemodialysis patients, higher serum phosphate was an independent risk factor for calciphylaxis after multivariable analysis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Single-centre retrospective matched case-control (20 haemodialysis cases, 40 controls matched on age and dialysis vintage), China

evidenceItems.summary: In the Japanese nationwide case-control study, serum phosphate and calcium-phosphate product were not significantly associated with biopsy-confirmed calciphylaxis in haemodialysis patients.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Japanese nationwide survey with case-control analysis: 28 definite (biopsy/clinical) haemodialysis calciphylaxis cases vs 56 age- and vintage-matched controls

evidenceItems.summary: In a small peritoneal dialysis case-control study, cumulative calcium carbonate (calcium salt) ingestion showed a trend toward increased calciphylaxis risk, which the authors interpreted as calcium ingestion being a risk factor.
evidenceItems.studySystem: University peritoneal dialysis centre; 8 CAPD calciphylaxis cases vs 37 controls matched on modality and dialysis vintage

evidenceItems.summary: In a large-dialysis-organisation matched case-control study (1030 incident CUA cases), higher serum calcium, phosphorus and parathyroid hormone at haemodialysis initiation were associated with later calciphylaxis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: US large dialysis organisation; 1030 incident haemodialysis CUA cases matched 1:2 on age, sex and race to 2060 controls; baseline factors at dialysis initiation

evidenceItems.summary: In the German calciphylaxis registry, median intact PTH in dialysis CUA patients was only moderately raised (147 pg/mL) and the authors concluded uncontrolled hyperparathyroidism is not the key determinant of calciphylaxis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: German nationwide internet-based registry, 2006-2015; 253 CUA patients (207 on dialysis), with central biobank

evidenceItems.summary: In the Japanese nationwide case-control study, higher adjusted serum calcium at diagnosis was associated with calciphylaxis in univariate analysis (warfarin and low albumin were the multivariable risk factors).
evidenceItems.studySystem: Japanese nationwide survey with case-control analysis: 28 definite haemodialysis calciphylaxis cases vs 56 matched controls

evidenceItems.summary: In the Mayo Clinic series, obesity was identified as a risk factor for calciphylaxis in dialysis patients compared with age- and sex-matched dialysis controls.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Mayo Clinic retrospective study; 64 calciphylaxis patients including 49 dialysis cases matched to 98 dialysis controls

evidenceItems.summary: In the same Mayo Clinic matched dialysis analysis, systemic corticosteroid use was associated with calciphylaxis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Mayo Clinic retrospective study; 49 dialysis calciphylaxis cases vs 98 age- and sex-matched dialysis controls

evidenceItems.summary: Diabetes was associated with later calciphylaxis in the large US dialysis case-control study, and insulin-treated patients showed a dose-response increase in odds of CUA at typical injection sites (abdomen/thigh).
evidenceItems.studySystem: US large dialysis organisation; 1030 incident haemodialysis CUA cases vs 2060 matched controls

evidenceItems.summary: In the Japanese nationwide case-control study, lower serum albumin remained a significant risk factor for calciphylaxis after multivariable adjustment.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Japanese nationwide survey with case-control analysis: 28 definite haemodialysis calciphylaxis cases vs 56 matched controls

evidenceItems.summary: In a US case-control study of end-stage kidney disease patients, women had about sixfold higher odds of calciphylaxis; low albumin and higher phosphate were also associated.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Single-centre case-control; 19 calciphylaxis cases (18 haemodialysis, 1 transplant) vs 54 controls matched on haemodialysis start date

evidenceItems.summary: In paired biopsies of lesional and clinically normal skin from 18 patients with suspected calciphylaxis (mostly dialysis), microvascular thrombosis was found only in lesional tissue.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human skin biopsies, lesional vs within-patient normal skin, 18 patients with suspected calciphylaxis (16 on dialysis)

evidenceItems.summary: Intimal hyperplasia of small arteries/arterioles was confined to lesional skin and, together with thrombosis and coarse vascular calcification, was judged a specific finding in suspected calciphylaxis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human skin biopsies, lesional vs within-patient normal skin, 18 patients with suspected calciphylaxis

evidenceItems.summary: Small-artery/arteriolar calcification was nearly as common in clinically normal skin as in lesional skin of the same patients; only coarse calcification was lesion-specific, so vascular calcification alone lacked specificity for necrotic lesions.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human skin biopsies, lesional vs within-patient normal skin, 18 patients with suspected calciphylaxis

evidenceItems.summary: Skin biopsies from patients with calciphylaxis (n=57) were significantly more likely than biopsies from ESRD patients without calciphylaxis (n=26) to show dermal vessel calcification and diffuse dermal thrombi; histology was indistinguishable between patients with and without CKD, suggesting a common pathway in uraemic and non-uraemic calciphylaxis.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Retrospective histopathology cohort: 57 calciphylaxis skin biopsies vs 26 biopsies from ESRD patients without calciphylaxis

evidenceItems.summary: Compared with viable skin from amputation margins of ESRD patients without calciphylaxis, skin biopsies taken for suspected calciphylaxis showed significantly more small-vessel thrombosis, whereas calcification prevalence did not differ overall.
evidenceItems.studySystem: 38 skin biopsies for suspected calciphylaxis vs 43 healthy-margin amputation specimens from ESRD patients without calciphylaxis; 2 autopsies

evidenceItems.summary: Medial calcification and other historically 'characteristic' findings also occurred in viable skin of ESRD patients without calciphylaxis; only the combination of medial calcification with thrombosis was rare in unaffected patients (six-fold more prevalent in high-suspicion biopsies).
evidenceItems.studySystem: 38 skin biopsies for suspected calciphylaxis vs 43 healthy-margin amputation specimens from ESRD patients without calciphylaxis

evidenceItems.summary: In a two-centre case-control study of patients with renal disease (38 calciphylaxis cases, 114 matched CKD controls), lupus anticoagulant, protein C deficiency and combined thrombophilias were more frequent in calciphylaxis cases.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Retrospective matched case-control (1:3 by age, sex, race), patients with CKD at two Boston academic hospitals

evidenceItems.summary: Restricting to stage 5 CKD, only lupus anticoagulant and combined thrombophilia remained associated with calciphylaxis (protein C deficiency did not), and in warfarin-unexposed patients only lupus anticoagulant and protein C deficiency remained; the associated thrombophilia component varies by subgroup.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Subgroup analysis of the matched case-control study (stage 5 CKD; warfarin-unexposed)

evidenceItems.summary: In a single-centre prospective series of 36 calciphylaxis cases, six-month mortality was 33% in patients presenting with non-ulcerating plaques and rose to above 80% once ulceration developed.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Single-centre prospective series of 36 dialysis patients with calciphylaxis (Canada)

evidenceItems.summary: In the UK Calciphylaxis Study, haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis had substantially higher all-cause mortality than propensity-matched haemodialysis patients without calciphylaxis (annual mortality 67% vs 10.2%).
evidenceItems.studySystem: UK national calciphylaxis registry (n=89), 62 haemodialysis patients vs propensity-matched CRISIS-HD haemodialysis cohort

evidenceItems.summary: In a 13-centre Malaysian dialysis cohort of 33 confirmed calciphylaxis cases, about half died within three months of diagnosis and septicaemia from infection was the most frequent cause of death.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Multicentre retrospective observational cohort, 33 dialysis patients with confirmed calciphylaxis, Malaysia 2016-2021

evidenceItems.summary: Sera from patients with uraemic calciphylaxis induced IL-6 and IL-6R synthesis in primary human dermal microvascular endothelial cells; TYMP-driven IL-6 activated tissue factor, a trigger of the extrinsic coagulation pathway, which anti-IL-6 treatment inhibited, and calciphylaxis skin showed increased IL-6 signalling.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Primary human dermal microvascular endothelial cells exposed to calciphylaxis patient sera, plus spatial analysis of calciphylaxis skin

evidenceItems.summary: In vitro, SNF472 bound hydroxyapatite with micromolar affinity, inhibited HAP crystal formation and inhibited calcification of rat vascular smooth muscle cells, with free-calcium chelation only at ~50-fold higher concentrations.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Cell-free HAP binding/crystallisation assays; excised rat vascular smooth muscle cells; dog and rat osteoblast/bone studies

evidenceItems.summary: In a single-arm open-label phase 2 study of 14 haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis, improvements from baseline in wound score (BWAT), pain and wound-related quality of life were observed after 12 weeks of SNF472.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Phase 2 open-label single-arm trial, 14 patients on thrice-weekly haemodialysis with calciphylaxis (NCT02790073)

evidenceItems.summary: In the phase 3 CALCIPHYX RCT (n=71), wound score (BWAT-CUA) and pain VAS improved similarly with hexasodium fytate and placebo at week 12 (BWAT-CUA LS mean difference 0.3, p=0.88; pain VAS difference 11.5, p=0.15); neither primary endpoint was met.
evidenceItems.studySystem: International phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial with open-label extension; adults on haemodialysis with ulcerated calciphylaxis lesion and pain VAS >=50 (NCT04195906)

evidenceItems.summary: In CALCIPHYX, deaths (1/38 vs 5/33 to week 12; 2/38 vs 7/33 over the whole trial) and calciphylaxis-related hospitalisations (2/38 vs 11/33) were fewer with hexasodium fytate than placebo, reported as serious adverse events rather than prespecified efficacy endpoints.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial with open-label extension (NCT04195906)

evidenceItems.summary: CALCIPHYX (NCT04195906) is registered as a completed phase 3 trial (71 enrolled, completed 2022-10-24) assessing SNF472 added to background care for calciphylaxis; supports investigational (experimental) status, not approval.
evidenceItems.location: ClinicalTrials.gov record field: descriptionModule.briefSummary; statusModule.overallStatus=COMPLETED; designModule.phases=PHASE3
evidenceItems.studySystem: ClinicalTrials.gov registry record

evidenceItems.summary: In uraemic rats, sodium thiosulfate prevented histological aortic calcification and reduced aortic, cardiac and renal calcium content, likely via acid- and/or chelation-induced urinary calcium loss; it also lowered bone strength.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Uraemic rat model (animal); aortic medial/vascular calcification

evidenceItems.summary: Sodium thiosulfate, acting as a hydrogen sulfide donor, inhibited intimal hyperplasia in mouse focal carotid stenosis models and in cultured human vein segments, limiting VSMC proliferation and migration via microtubule depolymerisation.
evidenceItems.studySystem: WT, LDLR-/- and Cse-/- mice with focal carotid stenosis; ex vivo human vein segments; primary human VSMCs

evidenceItems.summary: In 172 haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis treated with IV sodium thiosulfate (Fresenius Medical Care North America, 2006-2009), physician survey (n=53) reported complete resolution in 26.4% and improvement in a further 47.2%; one-year mortality was 35%. The authors state conclusive efficacy evidence is lacking.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Retrospective observational cohort of 172 maintenance haemodialysis patients with calciphylaxis treated with STS

evidenceItems.summary: A phase 3 placebo-controlled RCT of IV sodium thiosulfate for calciphylaxis pain (NCT03150420, Hope Pharmaceuticals) was terminated after enrolling 29, because patients could not be accrued without recent STS exposure; no results posted.
evidenceItems.studySystem: ClinicalTrials.gov registry record

evidenceItems.summary: Intravenous sodium thiosulfate 25 g thrice weekly is a placebo-controlled arm of the recruiting phase 3 BEAT-Calci platform trial (NCT05018221) in kidney failure with newly diagnosed calciphylaxis; supports experimental status.
evidenceItems.location: ClinicalTrials.gov record field: armsInterventionsModule.armGroups["Sodium Thiosulfate (Double-Blind Period)"].description; overallStatus=RECRUITING
evidenceItems.studySystem: ClinicalTrials.gov registry record

evidenceItems.summary: In the iPACK-HD pilot RCT (n=86 haemodialysis patients with coronary calcification), phylloquinone 10 mg thrice weekly for 12 months increased plasma phylloquinone and the Gla/Glu-osteocalcin ratio versus placebo, i.e. improved vitamin K status.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Multicentre randomised placebo-controlled pilot trial, haemodialysis patients with CAC >=30 AU (NCT01528800)

evidenceItems.summary: Phylloquinone supplementation in haemodialysis patients reduced inactive dephospho-uncarboxylated MGP by 86% versus placebo at 12 months, consistent with increased MGP carboxylation (activation); coronary calcification progression did not differ.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Multicentre randomised placebo-controlled pilot trial, haemodialysis patients with CAC >=30 AU (NCT01528800)

evidenceItems.summary: A pilot RCT of oral vitamin K in calciphylaxis (NCT02278692, MGH) is registered as completed (26 enrolled, 2019-08) with primary outcome change in circulating MGP, but has no posted results and no linked results publication was found.
evidenceItems.location: ClinicalTrials.gov record field: descriptionModule.briefSummary; overallStatus=COMPLETED; hasResults=false
evidenceItems.studySystem: ClinicalTrials.gov registry record

evidenceItems.summary: Oral vitamin K1 10 mg thrice weekly is a placebo-controlled arm of the recruiting phase 3 BEAT-Calci platform trial (NCT05018221); supports experimental status.
evidenceItems.location: ClinicalTrials.gov record field: armsInterventionsModule.armGroups["Vitamin K1 (Double-Blind Period)"].description; overallStatus=RECRUITING
evidenceItems.studySystem: ClinicalTrials.gov registry record

evidenceItems.summary: Calcimimetics such as cinacalcet act on the calcium-sensing receptor to lower parathyroid hormone without raising calcium and phosphorus (stated rationale of the phase 3 RCTs in haemodialysis patients).
evidenceItems.studySystem: Two identical phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials, 741 haemodialysis patients with uncontrolled secondary hyperparathyroidism

evidenceItems.summary: In placebo-controlled phase 3 RCTs in haemodialysis patients with uncontrolled secondary hyperparathyroidism, cinacalcet lowered PTH and improved calcium-phosphorus homeostasis over 26 weeks.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Two identical phase 3 randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trials (371 cinacalcet vs 370 placebo), haemodialysis

evidenceItems.summary: In a secondary analysis of adverse-event reports from the EVOLVE RCT (3861 haemodialysis patients with moderate-severe secondary hyperparathyroidism who received study drug), calciphylaxis occurred in 6 cinacalcet vs 18 placebo patients (unadjusted relative hazard 0.31, 95% CI 0.13-0.79).
evidenceItems.studySystem: Post hoc analysis of adverse-event reports in the EVOLVE phase 3 RCT (cinacalcet vs placebo), haemodialysis patients

evidenceItems.summary: Within the EVOLVE calciphylaxis cases, active vitamin K antagonist use was common (11 of 24 cases; 9 placebo, 2 cinacalcet) versus 5-7% of patients without calciphylaxis, so imbalance in VKA exposure between arms may confound the apparent cinacalcet effect.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Post hoc analysis of adverse-event reports in the EVOLVE phase 3 RCT

evidenceItems.summary: Circulating pyrophosphate was lower in 30 patients with calciphylaxis than in 30 matched controls; lower PPi was associated with higher odds of calciphylaxis after adjustment for ALP, phosphate and BMI.
evidenceItems.location: Main text, case-control results paragraph; table 1.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human calciphylaxis registry: 30 matched case-control pairs; 70-patient cohort, 67% ESKD. Fasting circulating PPi assay, predialysis in dialysis patients.

evidenceItems.summary: In the calciphylaxis cohort, lower enrollment PPi was associated with higher short-term mortality; PPi also correlated with lesion count but not pain intensity. These observations do not establish that raising PPi improves outcomes.
evidenceItems.location: Main text, cohort severity and mortality results paragraph.
evidenceItems.studySystem: Human calciphylaxis registry: 30 matched case-control pairs; 70-patient cohort, 67% ESKD. Fasting circulating PPi assay, predialysis in dialysis patients.

therapies.name: Hexasodium fytate (SNF472; CSL525)
therapies.modality: Small molecule (intravenous myo-inositol hexaphosphate salt) given during haemodialysis
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Binds hydroxyapatite (HAP) crystals and inhibits further HAP crystal formation/growth, the final common step of vascular calcification; selectivity for HAP over free-calcium chelation shown in vitro. Direct target is mapped to medial arteriolar calcification as the nearest shared entity (the molecular target is the mineral phase, not a protein).
therapies.indication: Investigational for calcific uraemic arteriolopathy (calciphylaxis) in patients on haemodialysis; no regulatory approval for calciphylaxis identified
therapies.jurisdiction: International (CALCIPHYX sites); not approved by any regulator for calciphylaxis as of 2026-10-10
therapies.trialPhase: Phase 3 completed (CALCIPHYX, NCT04195906): both primary endpoints not met
limitations: CALCIPHYX (n=71) did not show superiority over placebo on BWAT-CUA wound score or pain VAS at week 12.
Fewer deaths and calciphylaxis-related hospitalisations with drug were reported as serious adverse events, not as a prespecified efficacy endpoint; small numbers.
Phase 2 efficacy signal (n=14) was single-arm and uncontrolled.

No subsequent registered calciphylaxis trial found on ClinicalTrials.gov (search SNF472/CSL525/hexasodium fytate, 2026-10-10); sponsor pipeline status for this indication not verified, so status left experimental rather than withdrawn.
Sponsor-funded trials (Sanifit / CSL Vifor).

therapies.name: Sodium thiosulfate (intravenous)
therapies.modality: Small molecule (inorganic salt), intravenous, typically during haemodialysis
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Mechanism in calciphylaxis is uncertain. Preclinical data: in uraemic rats it prevented aortic calcification, attributed to acid- and/or chelation-induced urinary calcium loss; in mouse carotid-stenosis models and human vein segments it acted as a hydrogen sulfide donor that limited VSMC proliferation/migration and intimal hyperplasia. Targets are therefore recorded as indirect only (process-level effects shown outside human calciphylaxis); no direct molecular target is assigned.
therapies.indication: Calciphylaxis in patients on dialysis — off-label; no regulatory approval for calciphylaxis identified (approved labels are for other indications, e.g. cyanide poisoning; label not inspected in this branch)
therapies.jurisdiction: International off-label use; no regulator label for calciphylaxis identified
therapies.trialPhase: Phase 3 RCT terminated for poor accrual (NCT03150420); phase 3 platform arm recruiting (BEAT-Calci, NCT05018221); otherwise retrospective cohorts
limitations: No completed randomised placebo-controlled trial in calciphylaxis; efficacy evidence is uncontrolled observational.
Mechanistic evidence is from uraemic rat aortic calcification and mouse/human-vein intimal hyperplasia models, not human calciphylaxis.
Rat data showed reduced bone strength and metabolic acidosis.
Regulatory label not inspected; "off-label" statement rests on absence of any calciphylaxis approval identified.

therapies.name: Vitamin K1 (phylloquinone / phytonadione) supplementation
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Repletes vitamin K status, the cofactor for gamma-glutamyl carboxylation of matrix Gla protein; supplementation in haemodialysis patients lowers dephospho-uncarboxylated (inactive) MGP, i.e. increases active MGP, a calcification inhibitor.
therapies.indication: Calciphylaxis (treatment) in patients on dialysis — off-label; no regulatory approval for calciphylaxis identified; investigational
therapies.jurisdiction: US (MGH pilot RCT NCT02278692, completed, no results posted); international (BEAT-Calci NCT05018221, recruiting)
therapies.trialPhase: Pilot RCT completed without posted/published results (NCT02278692); phase 3 platform arm recruiting (NCT05018221)
limitations: No published efficacy result in calciphylaxis identified (Europe PMC and ClinicalTrials.gov checked 2026-10-10).
Biomarker (MGP carboxylation) evidence comes from haemodialysis patients with coronary calcification, not calciphylaxis; iPACK-HD showed no difference in coronary calcification progression.
Mechanistic rationale for calciphylaxis rests partly on observational MGP-carboxylation data (mechanism branch).

therapies.name: Cinacalcet
therapies.mechanismOfAction: Allosteric calcimimetic acting on the parathyroid calcium-sensing receptor, lowering parathyroid hormone without raising calcium and phosphorus.
therapies.indication: Calciphylaxis prevention/treatment — off-label; no regulatory approval for calciphylaxis identified (approved for secondary hyperparathyroidism on dialysis; label not inspected in this branch)
therapies.trialPhase: No calciphylaxis-specific trial; evidence is a secondary analysis of adverse-event reports from the phase 3 EVOLVE RCT
limitations: Calciphylaxis was not a prespecified EVOLVE endpoint; events came from adverse-event reports while on study drug (24 events among 3861 treated).
Unadjusted relative hazard; differential drug exposure/discontinuation can bias on-treatment analyses.
EVOLVE parent trial did not meet its primary cardiovascular endpoint in unadjusted ITT analysis.
Treatment (as opposed to prevention) of established calciphylaxis with cinacalcet supported only by case reports (not curated).
